summary.headline: Ganesh Consumer Q1 FY27 revenue fell 7.1% YoY to INR1,885 million, but EBITDA margin hit a record 11.2% and PAT rose 31.4% to INR125 million.
summary.overview: Revenue declined 7.1% YoY to INR1,885 million as heatwave, LPG shortages, benign wheat prices and assembly elections hit Eastern India demand. B2C fell 4.1% and B2B fell 17.9%, with B2B also reflecting a deliberate cut in low-margin volumes. EBITDA margin expanded to 11.2% (up 66 bps YoY, 313 bps QoQ), helped by procurement in a favourable commodity cycle, mix shift to value-added products and cost controls, despite ad spend rising to 3.1% of revenue from 1.9% in FY26. Management reiterated FY27 volume growth of 7-8% and an EBITDA margin of 9.8-10%, and pushed the Sattu/Besan plant commissioning to end of FY28.

financial_highlights.change: +66 bps YoY; +313 bps QoQ; highest in company history
vs 23 days in FY26 and 61 days in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Value-added and emerging products share of B2C revenue
financial_highlights.value: 68% (per MD opening remarks); c.59% per Q&A

segments.name: B2C (consumer-facing)
segments.commentary: Declined 4.1% YoY, held up better than B2B. Market share in packaged wheat-based category rose 1% and weighted distribution improved 1%. Atta share of B2C mix fell to about 32% from about 35% in FY26 as Sattu grew.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Declined 17.9% YoY, reflecting softer B2C volume pass-through, lower realisations and a deliberate exit from lower-margin volumes. One plant runs job work for a single unnamed FMCG client; Hyderabad plant also serves a B2B third-party packaging client.

segments.name: Spices
segments.commentary: Gross margin improved this quarter on better realisations and favourable product mix. Masala powders are 6-7% of revenue, targeted at 11-12% in about three years.

segments.name: Soya chunks (new)
segments.commentary: Distribution started this quarter. Management targets 2-3% of company revenue in two to three years, and pricing is currently aggressive, with margins expected to reach industry benchmark in 1.5-2 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth target of 7-8%; a firmer revenue view will come after Q2 (end of first half).
FY27 EBITDA margin guided to 9.8-10%, versus about 9.8% in FY26.
Gross margin to be better than FY26 levels; no exact percentage given.
Ethnic snacks and packaged sweets to be manufactured at Amta unit and launched in Q3 FY27; margins not disclosed but expected to be ahead of industry.
Sattu and Besan plant commissioning now expected towards end of FY28, behind original IPO timeline.
HoReCa segment expected to return to normal by end of Q2 FY27 after LPG-related disruption.
capex_capacity: Sattu and Besan manufacturing facility (IPO-funded): plant design in process; commissioning pushed to end of FY28 due to global supply chain and geopolitical delays.
Amta unit to manufacture ethnic snacks and packaged sweets.
Plan to add 300-400 distributors over the next two to three years, including over 50 added in Q1 FY27, for new geographies (Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Northeast) and new categories.
Geographic expansion: revenue from states other than West Bengal is about 7-8% today, targeted at 18-20% in two to three years.
demand_pricing: Q1 demand hit by extended heatwave, constrained LPG availability, benign wheat prices and assembly elections across Eastern India.
LPG price spike raised Sattu input costs; management absorbed the increase rather than passing it to consumers, citing brand pull and plant efficiencies.
Gross margin gain attributed mainly to better realisations and value-added mix; softer raw material prices contributed a small part, and value-added mix about 0.7-0.8% of gross margin.
Cash-and-carry model in general trade; B2B volume cut deliberately to protect margins.
Soya chunks priced aggressively at launch.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue expected from outside East India over the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus stays on Eastern India (Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Northeast) for the next two years; non-West Bengal share goes from about 7-8% to 18-20% in two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Margin profile of packaged sweets and snacks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give margin figures, but said backward integration (flour, gram flour, spices) and brand plus distribution should put margins ahead of industry.

qa_highlights.question: Why did atta share of B2C mix drop to 32% from 35%?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added segment, led by Sattu, grew; value-added and emerging share rose to about 59% from 56% in FY26. Atta mix expected to stay around 30-34%.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin split between mix and raw material prices?
qa_highlights.answer: RM softness was a small contributor; the main driver was better realisation and value-added mix, worth about 0.7-0.8%. No exact gross margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year revenue growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth target of 7-8%, with a firmer view after Q2; EBITDA margin guided to 9.8-10% versus about 9.8% last year.

qa_highlights.question: Soya chunks contribution and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected to reach 2-3% of company revenue in two to three years; margins to reach industry gross margin benchmark in 1.5-2 years as current pricing is aggressive.

risks_watch: Revenue is still declining; Q1 B2C and B2B both fell, so volume recovery needs to show in Q2.
Gross margin tailwind tied to a favourable commodity cycle and inventory build; cash conversion cycle rose to 43 days from 23 days in FY26.
LPG costs remain a risk for Sattu; the company absorbed the increase and has not passed it on.
Sattu/Besan plant delayed to end-FY28 with capex and revenue ramp deferred.
New categories (snacks, sweets, soya chunks) carry margin uncertainty, and management has not disclosed their margins or market size.
Ad spend at 3.1% of revenue may keep pressure on operating leverage.
Management gave unclear answers on B2B job work and did not disclose the TAM for new categories.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and brand strength, with record EBITDA margin highlighted. Cautious and somewhat vague on the top line, which declined, and on the delayed Sattu/Besan plant. Several answers were deferred or left unquantified (new-category margins, TAM, gross margin percentage, and whether to revisit the B2B contracting claim).
key_quotes: EBITDA margin expanded to 11.2%, the highest in the company's history, an improvement of 66 basis points year-on-year and 313 basis points sequentially.
The strategic rational for this investment, which is to expand our high-margin grain-based portfolio, remains fully intact and we will continue to keep investors apprised of progress on this front.
We plan to deliver in the range of 9.8% to 10% in the in the current financial year.

adds.what: Amta unit for ethnic snacks and packaged sweets (launch Q3 FY27)

growth.why: Management reiterates FY27 volume growth of 7-8% and EBITDA margin of 9.8-10% (vs ~9.8% in FY26), backed by mix shift, a 50+ distributor addition in Q1, and Amta unit snack launch in Q3 FY27, but the main Sattu/Besan capacity is pushed to end-FY28 and no firm revenue guide is given until after Q2.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin to 9.8-10% versus about 9.8% in FY26, and Q1 printed a record 11.2% (+66 bps YoY), though ad spend rose to 3.1% of revenue from 1.9% and part of the gain rests on a favourable commodity cycle.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Amta unit Q3 FY27; Sattu/Besan end FY28
rows.why: Sattu/Besan plant is deferred to end of FY28 (no near-term capacity), while the Amta unit for snacks and sweets launches in Q3 FY27 and 50+ distributors were added in Q1 against a 300-400 target over 2-3 years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterates 7-8% FY27 volume growth, but Q1 revenue fell 7.1% YoY (B2C -4.1%, B2B -17.9%) and the firmer revenue view comes only after Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure was disclosed and the one large capex (Sattu/Besan) has been pushed to end-FY28, so a fresh capex announcement in the window looks unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was only reiterated (volume 7-8%, EBITDA 9.8-10%) with no firmer revenue view until after Q2, and Q1 revenue declined 7.1%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue fell 7.1% YoY in Q1 and the 7-8% volume target needs a sharp recovery in Q2; B2B fell 17.9% and the Sattu/Besan plant slipped to end-FY28, and the margin tailwind depends on a favourable commodity cycle.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Ethnic snacks and packaged sweets are to be made at the Amta unit and launched in Q3 FY27, and soya chunks distribution started in Q1 with a 2-3% revenue target in 2-3 years.

rows.label: Geographic expansion beyond West Bengal
rows.why: Non-West Bengal revenue is about 7-8% today and targeted at 18-20% in two to three years, with Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and Northeast the focus, but no near-term number was given.

rows.label: Inventory and cash cycle normalisation
rows.why: Inventory days fell to 53 from 77 a year earlier and cash conversion cycle is 43 days versus 23 in FY26, so a build-up in inventory has been driving part of the margin gain and may reverse.

rows.label: HoReCa segment normalisation
rows.why: Management expects the HoReCa segment to return to normal by end Q2 FY27 after LPG-related disruption, which supports the volume recovery that the 7-8% target requires.

tone.note: Management was confident on record 11.2% EBITDA margin, brand strength and the 7-8% volume and 9.8-10% margin guide, but was cautious and vague on the 7.1% revenue decline, the Sattu/Besan delay to end-FY28, new-category margins and TAM, and the B2B job-work question.

quality.why: Revenue fell 7.1% YoY (B2C -4.1%, B2B -17.9%), so there is no headline growth to explain; the brief attributes the margin gain to better realisations and value-added mix, with softer raw material prices a small part, and it names no one-off items in the quarter.
